title: Preview and feature extraction
summary: Select an eye ROI, run the interactive MEYELens preview, and print pupil/eye feature samples from live camera frames.
description: This tutorial shows how to open an eye-facing camera, select a region of interest, tune the MEYELens segmentation preview, and extract geometric pupil and eye features from live frames.
imageAlt: MEYELens preview and feature extraction tutorial

sections.title: Goal
sections.body: Use the live preview to check that the camera, model, thresholds, masks, and feature overlays are working correctly. After closing the preview, the script collects 30 prediction samples and prints the extracted pupil and eye features.

sections.title: Requirements
items: MEYELens installed in a dedicated Python environment
Eye-facing camera connected to the computer
A visible and well-focused eye image
A selected region of interest around the eye

sections.title: What this script does
sections.body: The script creates a Meye segmentation object, opens the camera, lets you select the eye ROI, and starts the interactive preview. When you exit the preview, it acquires 30 frames, runs prediction on each frame, stores result.features, and prints the collected feature dictionaries.

sections.title: Feature output
items: valid: whether the mask contains positive pixels
area: number of pixels in the segmented mask
centroid: mean mask position in image coordinates
ellipse: fitted ellipse information for the largest mask contour
major_diameter and minor_diameter: fitted ellipse axes
orientation_deg: orientation of the major axis
ovality and eccentricity: shape elongation measures
major_axis and minor_axis: endpoints of the fitted ellipse axes

sections.title: Preview controls
sections.body: Use the interactive preview to tune the segmentation before collecting samples. You can adjust pupil and eye thresholds, toggle masks, toggle feature drawing, and print the current settings from the preview window.

sections.title: Camera index
sections.body: If the wrong camera opens, change `camera_index=0` to `camera_index=1` or `camera_index=2`.

sections.title: Invalid features
sections.body: If the pupil or eye is not clearly visible, some masks may be invalid and some ellipse values may be `NaN`. Improve focus, illumination, and ROI selection before collecting feature samples.

title: Use a custom model
summary: Load a custom MEYELens PyTorch model, preview segmentation on a selected eye ROI, and run prediction on a live camera frame.
description: This tutorial shows how to initialize MEYELens with a custom model file instead of the default model. The selected model path is saved in the MEYELens configuration, so future sessions will keep using it until another model is selected.

sections.title: Goal
sections.body: Use a custom MEYELens model for segmentation instead of the default model. This is useful when testing models from the [Model Zoo](software.html#model-zoo), evaluating a newly trained model, or comparing different model architectures on the same camera setup.

sections.title: Requirements
items: MEYELens installed in a dedicated Python environment
A compatible custom PyTorch model file, for example a .pt file
Eye-facing camera connected to the computer
A visible and well-focused eye image
A selected region of interest around the eye

sections.title: What this script does
sections.body: The script creates a Meye object using a custom model path, opens the camera, lets you select the eye ROI, and starts the interactive preview. After closing the preview, it acquires one frame, runs prediction with the custom model, and prints inference speed and extracted features.

sections.title: Model path
sections.body: Replace `path/to/your_custom_model.pt` with the actual path to your model file. The model path is saved in the MEYELens configuration file, so the same model will be used in future sessions unless you change it again.

sections.title: Preview before analysis
sections.body: Use the preview to check prediction quality before collecting data. This is especially important when comparing models trained with different architectures, input sizes, or datasets.

sections.title: Camera index
sections.body: If the wrong camera opens, change `camera_index=0` to `camera_index=1` or `camera_index=2`.

sections.title: Model compatibility
sections.body: Use a model file compatible with the current MEYELens PyTorch backend. If the model architecture or expected input format does not match the installed MEYELens version, loading or prediction may fail.

sections.title: Persistent model setting
sections.body: Because the selected model path is saved in the MEYELens configuration, future scripts may keep using the custom model. To restore the default model, initialize MEYELens again without a custom model path and reset the saved configuration with `meye = Meye(model_path=None)`, or manually remove the custom model path from the MEYELens configuration file.

title: Online MEYELens recording
summary: Record frame-level pupil and eye features from a live camera stream with synchronized trigger values.
description: This tutorial shows how to use MeyeRecorder to acquire camera frames, run MEYELens prediction online, save pupil and eye measurements, and attach trigger values to specific frames.

sections.title: Goal
sections.body: Record online pupil and eye measurements from the live camera stream. For each saved frame, MEYELens acquires the image, runs segmentation, extracts features, attaches trigger values, and writes one data row to disk.

sections.title: Requirements
items: MEYELens installed in a dedicated Python environment
Eye-facing camera connected to the computer
A visible and well-focused eye image
A selected region of interest around the eye
A MEYELens model configured and working in preview mode

sections.title: What this script does
sections.body: The script creates a Meye object, opens the camera, selects the eye ROI, and optionally runs the interactive preview to tune the segmentation. It then creates a MeyeRecorder, starts a recording session with metadata, saves 300 frames, and sends a one-frame trigger pulse on trg1 at frame 100.

sections.title: Saved output
items: Frame index
Frame timing information
Pupil centroid and area
Pupil ellipse features
Eye centroid and area
Eye ellipse features
Inference timing, when enabled
Trigger columns trg1 to trg9

sections.title: Metadata
sections.body: Use `recorder.start(metadata={...})` to save useful session information at the top of the output file, such as subject ID, condition, task name, session number, or acquisition notes.

sections.title: Triggers
sections.body: Trigger values passed to `save_frame()` are assigned to the same frame that is acquired and analyzed during that call. In this example, `trg1=1` only at frame 100 and is `0` for all other frames.

sections.title: Preview during recording
sections.body: Keep `show_preview=False` for better acquisition performance. Set `show_preview=True` only if you need to see the live MEYELens overlay while frames are being saved.

sections.title: Close the recorder
sections.body: Always call `recorder.close_all()` at the end of the acquisition. This stops the recording, flushes the buffered writer, closes the output file, and releases the camera resources.

sections.title: Invalid features
sections.body: If the pupil or eye is not detected clearly, some feature values may be invalid or contain `NaN`. Use the preview step to adjust thresholds, illumination, focus, and ROI selection before starting the recording.

title: Pupillary light reflex
summary: Run a pupillary light reflex experiment with PsychoPy, record online MEYELens features, and analyze stimulus-locked pupil responses.
description: This tutorial shows how to combine MEYELens with PsychoPy to present repeated light flashes, record synchronized pupil measurements and triggers, clean and filter the pupil trace, extract stimulus-locked epochs, and plot the pupillary light reflex.

sections.title: Goal
sections.body: Record a pupillary light reflex response using an eye-facing camera and a simple visual flash stimulus. The script saves online MEYELens pupil and eye features together with frame-level trigger values, then analyzes the pupil-area response around stimulus onset.

sections.title: Requirements
items: MEYELens installed in a dedicated Python environment
PsychoPy installed and working
Eye-facing camera connected to the computer
A visible and well-focused eye image
A selected region of interest around the eye
A MEYELens model configured and working in preview mode

sections.title: What this script does
sections.body: The script creates a `Meye` object, opens the camera, selects the eye ROI, and uses the interactive preview to tune segmentation. It then creates a PsychoPy window with a fixation dot and a white stimulus square. The recording follows a clear timing structure: an initial baseline period, followed by repeated trials with pre-stimulus, stimulus, and post-stimulus phases.

sections.title: Experiment timing
items: `BASELINE_SEC`: initial recording period before the trial sequence starts
`PRESTIM_SEC`: pre-stimulus period before each flash
`STIM_SEC`: duration of the white flash stimulus
`POSTSTIM_SEC`: post-stimulus recording period after each flash
`N_TRIALS`: number of repeated flash trials

sections.title: Trial structure
items: Initial baseline: fixation on a black screen, no trial trigger
Pre-stimulus: fixation on a black screen before each flash
Stimulus: white square appears on screen
Post-stimulus: fixation on a black screen after the flash
The full recording follows these timing parameters exactly, so epoch extraction can use the same pre- and post-stimulus windows

sections.title: Trigger structure
items: `trg1`: stimulus onset pulse, set to 1 only on the first frame of each flash
`trg2`: trial number, set to 0 during the initial baseline
`trg3`: stimulus state, set to 1 while the flash is visible and 0 otherwise

sections.title: Processing parameters
items: `DEBLINK_THRESHOLD`: derivative-based threshold used by `DeBlink` to detect blink-like artifacts
`DEBLINK_FLANKERS`: number of samples added around detected blink/artifact samples
`DEBLINK_REMOVE_ZEROS`: whether zero-valued pupil-area samples are treated as invalid
`FILTER_LOWCUT_HZ`: low cutoff frequency for pupil-trace filtering
`FILTER_HIGHCUT_HZ`: high cutoff frequency for pupil-trace filtering

sections.title: Epoch parameters
items: `EPOCH_TMIN`: start of the epoch relative to stimulus onset
`EPOCH_TMAX`: end of the epoch relative to stimulus onset
`EPOCH_BASELINE`: baseline interval used for baseline correction or z-score normalization
`EPOCH_TRANSFORM`: transform applied to the extracted epochs, for example `zscore`
`EPOCH_N_POINTS`: number of points used to resample each epoch for plotting and averaging

sections.title: Saved output
items: Frame timing information
Pupil area and centroid
Pupil ellipse features
Eye area and centroid
Eye ellipse features
Inference timing
Trigger columns for stimulus onset, trial number, and stimulus state
Metadata describing the experiment timing, processing parameters, epoch settings, and number of trials

sections.title: Analysis pipeline
sections.body: After recording, the script loads the saved file with `MeyeReader`, extracts the raw pupil-area trace, removes blinks and missing-pupil samples with `DeBlink`, estimates the sampling rate from frame timestamps, filters the cleaned pupil trace, and extracts epochs around the stimulus-onset trigger stored in `trg1`.

sections.title: Plots
items: Complete pupil-area trace with raw and cleaned/filtered signal
Vertical markers showing stimulus onset times
Single-trial pupillary light reflex epochs
Average baseline-corrected pupil response
Shaded region showing the stimulus duration

sections.title: Preview before recording
sections.body: Use the MEYELens preview before starting the experiment to adjust pupil and eye thresholds. Reliable segmentation during preview will make the recorded pupil-area trace easier to clean and analyze.

sections.title: Stimulus onset trigger
sections.body: The analysis uses `trg1` to find stimulus onset. Keep `trg1=1` only on the first frame of the flash, not during the full flash duration.

sections.title: Stimulus state
sections.body: Use `trg3` to store whether the flash is currently visible. This is useful for checking stimulus timing and verifying that the stimulus duration was correctly recorded.

sections.title: Epoch timing
sections.body: Keep `EPOCH_TMIN` within the available pre-stimulus period and `EPOCH_TMAX` within the available post-stimulus period. In this script, `EPOCH_TMIN` and `EPOCH_TMAX` are defined from `PRESTIM_SEC` and `POSTSTIM_SEC` to keep recording and analysis aligned.

sections.title: Display brightness
sections.body: The strength of the pupillary light reflex depends on screen brightness, ambient illumination, viewing distance, and stimulus size. Keep these conditions stable across participants and sessions.

sections.title: Safe shutdown
sections.body: The script uses a `try/finally` block to stop the recorder and close the PsychoPy window even if the experiment is interrupted. Keep this structure when adapting the script.

sections.title: Invalid pupil samples
sections.body: Blinks, poor focus, bad illumination, or inaccurate ROI selection can produce missing or invalid pupil-area values. The analysis removes zero-valued samples and blink-like artifacts before filtering and epoch extraction.

title: Visual oddball task
summary: Run a visual oddball experiment with PsychoPy, record online MEYELens features, behavioral responses, and stimulus triggers.
description: This tutorial shows how to combine MEYELens with PsychoPy to present standard, target, and distractor gratings while recording synchronized pupil measurements, stimulus events, and spacebar responses.

sections.title: Goal
sections.body: Record pupil dynamics during a visual oddball task. The participant fixates a central red dot while brief gratings are presented. Standard gratings require no response, oddball target gratings require a SPACE response, and distractor gratings require no response.

sections.title: Requirements
items: MEYELens installed in a dedicated Python environment
PsychoPy installed and working
Eye-facing camera connected to the computer
A visible and well-focused eye image
A selected region of interest around the eye
A MEYELens model configured and working in preview mode

sections.title: What this script does
sections.body: The script generates a visual oddball sequence with standards, oddball targets, and distractors. It opens the camera, selects the eye ROI, runs the MEYELens preview, shows task instructions with example stimuli, records the experiment with MeyeRecorder, stores behavioral responses, and analyzes the pupil trace after the task.

sections.title: Stimulus conditions
items: Standard: 0 degree grating, no response required
Oddball target: +45 degree grating, press SPACE
Distractor: -45 degree grating, no response required

sections.title: Trigger structure
items: trg1: stimulus onset code, with 1=standard, 2=oddball, and 3=distractor
trg2: trial number
trg3: stimulus visibility state, set to 1 while the grating is visible
trg4: behavioral response, set to 1 on frames where SPACE is detected

sections.title: Task timing
items: Initial fixation-only period before stimulation
A few initial standard trials
Random standard, oddball, and distractor trials
Minimum number of standards enforced between rare events
Final fixation-only period after stimulation

sections.title: Saved output
items: Frame timing information
Pupil area and centroid
Pupil ellipse features
Eye area and centroid
Eye ellipse features
Inference timing
Stimulus and response trigger columns
Experiment metadata describing task timing, orientations, and trigger meanings

sections.title: Behavior output
sections.body: During the task, the script stores one behavioral row per trial with trial number, trial type, whether the participant responded, response time, and correctness. At the end, it prints response rate and accuracy separately for standards, oddballs, and distractors.

sections.title: Analysis pipeline
sections.body: After recording, the script loads the saved file with MeyeReader, extracts the pupil-area trace, removes blinks and missing-pupil samples with DeBlink, estimates the sampling rate from frame timestamps, filters the cleaned trace, builds one trigger vector per condition, and extracts stimulus-locked epochs.

sections.title: Plots
items: Complete pupil-area trace with raw and cleaned/filtered signal
Vertical markers showing detected stimulus onsets
Average pupil response for standards, oddballs, and distractors
SEM band around the mean response for each condition

sections.title: Preview before recording
sections.body: Use the MEYELens preview before starting the task to tune pupil and eye thresholds. Reliable segmentation during preview will improve the quality of the recorded pupil-area trace.

sections.title: Event coding
sections.body: Keep `trg1` as a one-frame stimulus onset code. The analysis uses this column to separate standards, oddballs, and distractors into different epoch groups.

sections.title: Response coding
sections.body: Use `trg4` to mark SPACE responses in the frame-level recording. The script also keeps a separate trial-level behavior list for response rate, response time, and accuracy.

sections.title: Task instructions
sections.body: Make sure the participant understands that only the +45 degree grating requires a SPACE response. Responses to standards or distractors are counted as incorrect.

sections.title: Timing and display
sections.body: Stimulus timing depends on the display refresh rate, PsychoPy timing, and system performance. Keep the setup stable across sessions and avoid running heavy background processes during the experiment.

sections.title: Invalid pupil samples
sections.body: Blinks, eye movements, poor focus, bad illumination, or inaccurate ROI selection can produce missing or invalid pupil-area values. The analysis removes zero-valued samples and blink-like artifacts before filtering and epoch extraction.

title: Raw eye-video recording
summary: Record the raw eye-camera stream and save synchronized frame-level trigger values without running MEYELens segmentation.
description: This tutorial shows how to use EyeVideoRecorder to save a raw eye video together with a trigger/timing CSV file. It is useful when you want lightweight acquisition and plan to run pupil or eye analysis offline later.

sections.title: Goal
sections.body: Record the eye-facing camera stream as a raw video while saving one synchronized trigger and timing row for each saved frame. This script does not create a Meye object and does not run online pupil or eye segmentation.

sections.title: Requirements
items: MEYELens installed in a dedicated Python environment
Eye-facing camera connected to the computer
A visible and well-focused eye image
A selected region of interest around the eye
Enough disk space for the raw video file

sections.title: What this script does
sections.body: The script opens the camera with the requested frame rate and resolution, lets you select the eye ROI, creates an EyeVideoRecorder, starts a timestamped recording session, saves 300 video frames, writes trigger values for each successfully saved frame, and then closes the recorder safely.

sections.title: Saved output
items: A timestamped session folder in the standard MEYELens data directory
video.mp4 containing the raw eye-camera movie
triggers.csv containing one timing and trigger row per saved frame
Metadata written at the top of triggers.csv as comment lines

sections.title: Example trigger structure
items: trg1: example event pulse, set to 1 only at frame 100
trg2: current frame number
trg3: example block or condition code

sections.title: When to use this recorder
sections.body: Use EyeVideoRecorder when you want to save raw eye videos for later offline analysis, avoid online model inference during acquisition, keep recording as fast and lightweight as possible, or synchronize frame-wise triggers with the saved video.

sections.title: ROI selection
sections.body: The selected ROI is applied automatically to every frame returned by `cam.get_frame()`. This means that the saved video contains the cropped eye region rather than the full camera frame.

sections.title: Performance
sections.body: Because this recorder does not call `Meye.predict()`, it is lighter than online segmentation recording. It is a good option when timing and acquisition stability are more important than immediate pupil measurements.

sections.title: Preview during recording
sections.body: Set `show_preview=True` to display the raw camera image while recording. For maximum performance, set `show_preview=False` once the camera position and ROI are stable.

sections.title: No online pupil features
sections.body: This recorder saves only the raw video and trigger/timing table. It does not save pupil area, centroid, ellipse features, masks, or inference timing because no MEYELens prediction is performed during recording.

sections.title: Dropped or missing frames
sections.body: A trigger row is written only when a frame is successfully acquired and written to the video. Check the return value of `recorder.save_frame()` to detect failed frame acquisition.

sections.title: Close the recorder
sections.body: Always close the recorder with `recorder.close_all()`. This flushes and closes the trigger CSV file and releases the video writer. The camera is released automatically by the `with Camera(...)` block.

title: Eye-image dataset collector
summary: Collect raw eye snapshots, prediction-overlay snapshots, raw movies, and overlay movies for dataset creation.
description: This tutorial shows how to use the camera and MEYELens prediction loop to build eye-image datasets. It supports saving raw frames, mask-overlay frames, raw movies, prediction-overlay movies, and metadata describing the acquisition settings.

sections.title: Goal
sections.body: Collect eye-image material that can be used for dataset building, visual inspection, model testing, or later annotation. The script runs MEYELens prediction live, but the saved data can include either clean raw camera images or prediction-overlay images.

sections.title: Requirements
items: MEYELens installed in a dedicated Python environment
Eye-facing camera connected to the computer
A visible and well-focused eye image
Optional ROI selection around the eye
Enough disk space for image snapshots and video files

sections.title: What this script does
sections.body: The script creates a timestamped dataset session folder, opens the camera, runs MEYELens prediction on each frame, displays a live preview with pupil and eye masks, and lets you save snapshots or movies using keyboard commands.

sections.title: Saved output
items: raw_snapshots: PNG images from the clean camera stream
overlay_snapshots: PNG images with pupil and eye mask overlays
raw_movies: video files containing the clean camera stream
overlay_movies: video files containing the prediction mask overlay
metadata.csv: acquisition settings and information for each saved file

sections.title: Keyboard controls
items: s: save raw PNG snapshot
S: save prediction-overlay PNG snapshot
r: start or stop raw movie recording
R: start or stop prediction-overlay movie recording
+ or =: increase pupil threshold
- or _: decrease pupil threshold
]: increase eye threshold
[: decrease eye threshold
p: toggle pupil mask
o: toggle eye mask
h: print commands
q or ESC: quit

sections.title: Metadata
sections.body: For every saved snapshot or completed movie, the script appends one row to metadata.csv. The row includes file type, filename, image size, camera index, target FPS, crop information, pupil and eye thresholds, mask visibility settings, and recording duration for movies.

sections.title: Prediction overlay
sections.body: The overlay view draws only the pupil and eye masks. It does not draw centroids, ellipses, axis points, or feature text, making the saved overlay images cleaner for dataset inspection and documentation.

sections.title: Raw versus overlay files
sections.body: Use raw snapshots and raw movies when you want clean images for annotation or training. Use prediction-overlay snapshots and movies when you want to visually inspect current model performance.

sections.title: Threshold tuning
sections.body: Adjust the pupil and eye thresholds while previewing the live stream. The current threshold values are stored in metadata.csv when you save snapshots or stop movie recordings.

sections.title: ROI option
sections.body: Set `USE_ROI=True` if you want to manually crop the eye region before collecting data. The selected crop is then applied to every frame returned by the camera.

sections.title: Prediction is used during collection
sections.body: Unlike raw video recording, this collector calls `Meye.predict()` on every frame to generate the live mask overlay. This is useful for model inspection, but it is heavier than recording raw video only.

sections.title: Movie finalization
sections.body: A movie is written to metadata.csv only when recording is stopped normally with `r` or `R`. If the script is interrupted while a movie is still recording, the video writer is released, but no final duration row may be appended.

sections.title: Dataset consistency
sections.body: For training datasets, keep camera settings, illumination, focus, ROI strategy, and file naming consistent across sessions. Use metadata.csv to track acquisition conditions.

title: One-camera gaze calibration
summary: Calibrate a simple one-camera gaze estimator from MEYELens pupil and eye features, then test live gaze prediction on screen.
description: This tutorial shows how to collect fixation samples with PsychoPy targets, train a gaze calibration model from MEYELens features, and display a live filtered gaze pointer using a single eye-facing camera.

sections.title: Goal
sections.body: Estimate gaze position from one eye-facing camera by calibrating MEYELens pupil and eye features against known screen target positions. After calibration, the script predicts gaze coordinates online and displays a live gaze pointer.

sections.title: Requirements
items: MEYELens installed in a dedicated Python environment
PsychoPy installed and working
Eye-facing camera connected to the computer
A visible and well-focused eye image
A selected region of interest around the eye
Stable head position during calibration and testing
A MEYELens model configured and working in preview mode

sections.title: What this script does
sections.body: The script creates a Meye model, an AdaptiveGazeFilter, and a MeyeGazeCalibrator. It opens a PsychoPy window, shows calibration targets one at a time, collects multiple valid MEYELens samples for each target, fits a gaze model, and then starts a live prediction loop with a filtered green gaze dot.

sections.title: Calibration settings
items: MODEL_TYPE: calibration model used for mapping eye features to screen coordinates
NUM_POINTS: number of calibration target positions
FIXATION_DELAY_SEC: delay after target onset before collecting samples
SAMPLES_PER_TARGET: number of valid MEYELens samples collected for each target
SCREEN_WIDTH and SCREEN_HEIGHT: PsychoPy coordinate range used by the calibrator

sections.title: Supported calibration models
items: ridge_poly: polynomial ridge regression
ridge: linear ridge regression
mlp: multilayer perceptron regressor

sections.title: Calibration procedure
sections.body: For each target, the dot first appears in red during the fixation delay. When sample collection starts, the dot turns green. The script then acquires camera frames, runs MEYELens prediction, and adds only valid pupil/eye feature samples to the calibrator.

sections.title: Model fitting
sections.body: After all calibration targets are completed, the script fits the selected model with `calibrator.fit()`. In this example, samples are aggregated with the median for each target before fitting, which helps reduce the influence of noisy frames.

sections.title: Live prediction
sections.body: During the live test, each new camera frame is processed with MEYELens and passed to `calibrator.predict_xy()`. If the current frame has invalid features, the script keeps the last valid gaze prediction instead of moving the pointer to an invalid position.

sections.title: Use preview first
sections.body: Run the MEYELens preview before calibration to tune pupil and eye thresholds. Good segmentation during preview is essential for stable gaze calibration.

sections.title: Collect enough samples
sections.body: Increase `SAMPLES_PER_TARGET` if predictions are noisy. More samples per target make the median feature estimate more stable, but calibration takes longer.

sections.title: Smooth the pointer
sections.body: The AdaptiveGazeFilter reduces jitter in the live gaze dot. Lower `min_cutoff` gives stronger smoothing, while higher `beta` makes the pointer respond faster during larger gaze shifts.

sections.title: Head stability
sections.body: This example uses one eye-facing camera and does not explicitly compensate for head movement. Keep the head and camera position stable during calibration and testing. A **chin rest** is highly recommended.

sections.title: Calibration quality
sections.body: Poor ROI selection, bad focus, reflections, blinks, or unstable fixation can produce invalid features and inaccurate gaze predictions. Repeat calibration if the live pointer is systematically shifted or unstable.

sections.title: Coordinate system
sections.body: The script uses PsychoPy `norm` coordinates. Target and gaze positions are expressed in the same screen coordinate system, not in pixels.
